Callimachus: the catalogue for your AI coding history
Named for Callimachus, who built the first catalogue of the Library of Alexandria.

Grab the latest signed build from **Releases**: macOS (`.dmg`, Apple Silicon), Windows (`.msi` or `-setup.exe`), or Linux (`.AppImage`, `.deb` or `.rpm`). The app auto-updates from there on. Prefer to build it yourself? See Develop.

- **Indexes** every conversation from 13 coding agents into one local SQLite store: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor (the editor's chats, its agent transcripts and the Cursor CLI), Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, Goose, OpenCode, Continue, Cline, Roo Code, Kilo Code, Copilot Chat (the built-in chat panel of VS Code, Cursor, VSCodium and Windsurf), and the Copilot CLI. Adding another source is a small, documented contract.

- **Links threads to commits**: infers **on-device** which git commits a thread produced, by overlapping the files a thread discussed with `git log`'s changed files inside the thread's time window (shared-file count = confidence). See it as a thread→commit timeline (`cal commits`), per-thread in the desktop UI ("Produced commits"), or via the `linked_commits` MCP tool. Run it backwards from code with `cal why <file>:<line>`: `git blame` names the commit behind the line, and you get the sessions that produced it (the ones that edited the file first) with their decisions and gotchas; the same answer comes from `threads_for_file` with a `line`, and from **Why This Line** in the VS Code / Cursor extension, which also marks the lines a session wrote in the gutter and explains them on hover. It speaks Agent Trace (an open RFC for AI code attribution) both ways: when a repo carries trace records in `.agent-trace/`, `cal why` and `threads_for_file` show the agent, model and conversation another tool recorded for a line, even one Callimachus has no transcript of, and `cal trace export` writes records for the commits your sessions produced. The background watcher links new sessions' commits as they are indexed, and records which files each session read, edited or wrote from its tool calls (sessions indexed before the update are filled in once, in the background).

- **Stays current** via a background file watcher, plus a catch-up pass at launch for the sessions your agents wrote while the app was closed; **stays private**: the index never leaves your machine, API keys live in the OS keychain, conversation content goes only to an AI provider you pick, and usage analytics are opt-in and content-free (see Security & privacy).
This is a Turborepo + pnpm workspace.

**Claude Code plugin**: the one-step setup for Claude Code. It bundles the `/recall` skill (as `/callimachus:recall`), the MCP server (the `callimachus-mcp` launcher ships inside the plugin and runs with `node`, pinned to the plugin's release) and the SessionStart, PreCompact and SessionEnd memory hooks (plugins/claude-code):

The hooks run the `cal` CLI at `~/.local/bin/cal`, so open the desktop app (which builds the index) and click **Install the cal CLI** in **Settings → Agents** once (the Claude Code button's label while the plugin is enabled): that installs only `cal` and removes the app's own skill, MCP entry and hooks, so memory is never injected twice and only one server starts; Settings then says the integration is managed by the plugin. Until `cal` exists the hooks do nothing. **Without the desktop app** (macOS and Linux), `npx callimachus-mcp --install-cal` downloads the release's `cal` (checked against the same `SHA256SUMS` as the MCP server) and links it at `~/.local/bin/cal`; run `cal index` once to build the index, and from then on the plugin's SessionStart hook (`cal index --if-stale`) starts a catch-up pass in the background whenever the index is more than an hour old and neither the app nor `cal watch` keeps it fresh. You give up the app's windows (the Projects page, Chat, the harvest controls and Settings, where memory distillation is turned on); search, recall, the memory hooks and the MCP server work the same (plugins/claude-code). The plugin needs the app at 0.11.4 or later: the marketplace serves it from the latest release tag, with the MCP server pinned to that release, so keep the app on the latest release too. **On Windows, use Settings → Agents instead of the plugin**: Claude Code runs plugin hooks through Git Bash (or PowerShell, where they fail with a hook error), and the app keeps its own skill, MCP entry and hooks there, so the plugin would load them twice.

Install it from the Cursor Marketplace once it is listed there (**Customize**, search for Callimachus), or until then copy `plugins/cursor` into `~/.cursor/plugins/local/callimachus` and reload the window. On cursor.directory, **Add to Cursor** adds only the MCP server. Alongside the app's own Cursor hooks (Settings → Agents) the memory still arrives once per chat: `cal hook --for cursor` claims each conversation with a marker under `~/.callimachus/recall`. **On Windows, use Settings → Agents instead**: the plugin's hooks are `sh` scripts.

**MCP server**: let any agent search its own past work mid-session. It reads the index the desktop app builds and does not index anything by itself, so install the app and let it index once first (or, without the app, run `cal index`; see below). The quickest way to register it is `npx` (it downloads the prebuilt binary on first run and verifies its SHA-256); it's also listed on the official MCP registry as `io.github.BetaBots-LLC/callimachus`:

Already running the desktop app? You don't need npm: **Settings → Agents → Enable for Claude Code** registers the app itself (launched with `--mcp`) as Claude Code's MCP server, and **Settings → Agents → Other agents** does the same for Codex, Cursor and Gemini CLI. The app keeps those entries pointed at itself after an update or a move. You can also download the standalone `callimachus-mcp-<target>` binary from Releases, or build from a checkout with `cargo install --locked --path apps/desktop/src-tauri/standalone --bin callimachus-mcp` (add `--force` over a source install from an earlier version).

Tools (23), read **and** write. Reads (18): `search_threads`, `search_current_project` (auto-scoped to the repo it runs in), `recent_threads`, `get_thread`, `list_tags`, `list_open_todos`, `get_thread_knowledge`, `recall_decisions`, `recall_gotchas`, `find_prior_work` (the "have I done this before?" guard: prior sessions similar to a task), `project_memory` (a project's aggregated decisions / gotchas / open TODOs), `ask_history` (a cited RAG answer over your history), `threads_for_file` (which sessions touched a path; with a `line`, the commits behind it and the decisions of the sessions that wrote them), `check_decision` (surface settled decisions before re-litigating a proposal), `linked_commits` (the commits a thread likely produced), `recurring_issues` (errors you keep hitting across sessions), `list_snapshots` (a project's session snapshots), and `load_snapshot` (restore a saved checkpoint). Writes (5, into Callimachus's own memory, never your code): `complete_todo` (close an open TODO), `record_decision` (optionally with a `rationale`, and `replaces` when it reverses a recalled decision), `record_gotcha` (persist a fact into a project's memory), `flag_fact` (mark a recalled fact stale or wrong, which keeps it out of memory until you review it; capped per project, limited to the repo the server runs in, and a fact you pinned or edited stays in), and `snapshot_session` (checkpoint a thread for handoff). The bundled `/recall` skill (resources/recall/SKILL.md) tells agents when to reach for them.

Every tool also declares an `outputSchema` and returns `structuredContent` that matches it, which is what Claude Code and Codex hand the model: a list sits under a key (`{"threads": [...]}`, `{"facts": [...]}`), markdown under `markdown`, and an answer that is guidance instead of results (no index yet, a version skew, a busy write, no embedding model) is `{"notice": "..."}`, which every tool's schema allows. The text block is unchanged for every client except `check_decision`'s, which lists each prior decision with its status, date and `[thread N]` (and what replaced a superseded one), so a client that reads only the text cannot take a reversed decision for a settled one; clients older than MCP 2025-06-18 get no structured content. The output schemas are checked in under `schemas/mcp/` (served at `https://callimachus.app/schemas/mcp/<tool>.json`) and a test fails when one drifts. `get_thread` and `load_snapshot` carry the transcript in both the text and `markdown`, so their response is about twice `budget`.

**CLI**: `cal`, pipe-friendly. The desktop app installs it with **Settings → Agents → Enable for Claude Code**: on macOS and Linux it is linked at `~/.local/bin/cal` (if `~/.local/bin` isn't on your shell's `PATH`, as on stock macOS, Settings shows the `export PATH=...` line to add), and on Windows it is placed as `cal.exe` next to the app. If another program already owns `~/.local/bin/cal`, or a per-machine Windows install can't write `cal.exe`, Callimachus leaves `cal` out and says so in Settings; the hooks, MCP server and `/recall` skill work without it. You can also run `npx callimachus-mcp --install-cal` (macOS and Linux), which downloads the release's `cal` and links it at `~/.local/bin/cal` (never over another program's `cal`), download the standalone `cal-<target>` binary from Releases, or build from a checkout with `cargo install --locked --path apps/desktop/src-tauri/standalone --bin cal` (add `--force` over a source install from an earlier version).

**`--json-version 1` is the versioned contract** for scripts and tools (the VS Code extension asks for it). With it (or `CAL_JSON_VERSION=1` in the environment beside `--json`), the outputs of `search`, `recent`, `related`, `cat`, `stats`, `memory`, `decisions`, `gotchas`, `commits`, `why`, `trace`, `cost`, `report`, `issues`, `audit-pr` and `doctor` open with `schema_version` (now `1`); a list comes as `{"schema_version": 1, "results": [...]}` and an object keeps its fields next to the version. When `decisions` or `gotchas` can't run (no embedding model on the machine), the list is empty and a `notice` says why. Each versioned output has a JSON Schema at `https://callimachus.app/schemas/cal/<command>.v1.json` (in the repo, `schemas/cal/`), generated from the Rust types: a test fails when the two drift. A new field can appear within a version, so ignore fields you don't know; removing or renaming one, or changing its type, bumps the version, and a reader should refuse a version newer than it was written for. Plain `--json` still prints the bare arrays and objects it always has, so existing scripts keep working, but that shape is unversioned and may change in a future major release.

**VS Code / Cursor**: the extension adds a "Callimachus History" sidebar, a status-bar search button, commands to search / insert / copy threads, and **Why This Line** (editor context menu) for the sessions behind the line under the cursor (it shells out to `cal`). O SIMPA é dividido em serviços independentes, cada um no seu container e com o próprio banco (D13). Tudo sobe com um único comando do Docker Compose.
|`gateway`|Única porta de entrada; encaminha `/api/<serviço>/` e gera o `X-Request-ID`|RF12, RNF15|
|`frontend`|Interface web em React (D12)|RF04, RF06, RNF11, RNF12|
|`auth`|Login, emissão de JWT (RS256), usuários e perfis|RF09, D03, D15|
|`academico`|Turmas, disciplinas, alunos, inscrições, notas e frequência|RF01–RF04, RF08, D10|
|`analitico`|Painel, indicadores, interpretação automática, predição por regressão, recomendações, histórico de risco e relatórios|RF05–RF07, RF11, D21|
|`academico-despachante`|Publica no RabbitMQ os eventos gravados na outbox do acadêmico, com confirmação do broker. **Sem ele nenhum evento sai**|RF03, D14|
|`analitico-worker`|Consome os eventos, recalcula o risco, ignora repetidos e manda o que falhou para a fila de falhas|RF03, D11, D14|
|Interface|React + Vite + TypeScript, Recharts, Lucide, fonte Inter|
|Análise|`Decimal` (estatística e risco), numpy (regressão), openpyxl e reportlab (relatórios)|

Os painéis ficam só em `127.0.0.1`. Os alertas vão para um receptor local de teste; para e-mail ou chat é preciso definir o canal. O que fazer em cada alerta está em docs/operacao-filas.md.
